title: Improving Workflow Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain the key behavior of improving workflow performance and identify when it should be used.
Configure or review the workflow fields and permissions relevant to improving workflow performance.
Verify the result using a controlled run or static check and interpret the evidence.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on improving workflow performance. Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change. Use the example to predict the workflow result, then verify the behavior in a safe test repository or by static review.
content.why_it_matters: Improving Workflow Performance matters because it affects correctness, security, maintainability, or operating cost. Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change. Optimize from measured workflow duration and usage. Remove redundant work, cache only rebuildable dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and keep retry behavior bounded.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change. Optimize from measured workflow duration and usage. Remove redundant work, cache only rebuildable dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and keep retry behavior bounded. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Removing unnecessary steps
items.text: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

items.title: Parallelizing independent work
items.text: List the supported combinations explicitly and use `include`/`exclude` or `max-parallel` to control expansion. Keep all required configurations covered and avoid unnecessary duplicate jobs.

items.title: Reusing dependencies
items.text: For reusing dependencies, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Right-sizing matrices
items.text: For right-sizing matrices, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Reducing redundant builds
items.text: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.

items.title: Improving expensive test stages
items.text: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. Include shared dependencies and test the changed and unchanged path cases so required checks are not bypassed.

content_blocks.code:
jobs:
  internal-check:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - run: echo "Route only trusted workloads to this runner group"
content_blocks.expected_output: The job requests a runner matching the configured labels and applies a timeout; actual availability/access depend on runner registration and policy.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a test repository or static validation first. Confirm the snippet matches the repository, runner, permissions, and current GitHub documentation.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Remove temporary test workflows and never carry test credentials or sample outputs into production.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to improving workflow performance. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. Record the difference between your prediction and the actual result. Do not add production secrets or grant write permissions just to make a sample pass.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

items.title: Permissions and trust
items.text: Start with read-only access. If the example needs more access, explain the exact operation and reduce permissions again afterwards.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain improving workflow performance, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Improve reliability and latency using measurements rather than assumptions.

content.task: Apply improving workflow performance to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.
hints: Start with the key behavior: Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change.
Inspect the exact event filters, permissions, expressions, inputs, and job dependencies that affect this example.
Compare the observed status and logs with the expected result; distinguish static validation from a real hosted run.
content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
summary: Measure before optimizing: eliminate redundant steps, cache dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and compare run duration and cost after each change.
Optimize from measured workflow duration and usage. Remove redundant work, cache only rebuildable dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and keep retry behavior bounded.
Use the provided example as a starting point, replace placeholders with repository-specific checks, and validate both success and expected failure behavior before publication.
